avoid: Colliding with opposing dancers across the line
children.counts: Four counts of preparation followed by four counts of jumping.
children.game_version: A mirror-jumping partner game where children face each other in two lines and take turns leading leaps while matching jump heights.

avoid: Deep knee bends or hard landings
seniors.seated_version: Perform seated rhythmic torso lifts and alternating heel stomps to match the drum cadence, accompanied by forward-reaching courtship arm gestures.
seniors.standing_version: Gentle calf raises and knee bends in place without leaving the ground, maintaining steady alignment while facing a partner.
seniors.tempo_and_range: Keep tempo moderate; restrict movement range to low-impact ankle flexion and shallow knee bends.

movement_profile.footwork: Two-footed takeoff and landing executing continuous high vertical jumps facing an opposing line.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Two opposing linear ranks positioned facing each other in an open communal space.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Torso held firm and upright to support elevation during vertical leaps.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Emphasis on aerial elevation through high vertical jumps from ground level.
movement_profile.partnering: Opposing line formation where women initiate partner selection by choosing their male counterparts.
movement_profile.posture: Upright, alert vertical posture aligned for explosive upward propulsion.

signature_moves.description: A vigorous vertical jump performed while directly facing an opposing partner across the dancing lines.
signature_moves.name: High courtship leap

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Energetic and buoyant, aligned with celebratory post-harvest jumping.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid stiff-legged landings or collapsing forward at the waist; ensure joint absorption on each descent.

music_profile.sound_description: The sonic signature is driven by the acoustic resonance of the adungu harp intertwined with the rhythmic, grounded beat of the ngoma drum and the sharp, rustling percussion of the ekitirikiti.

basic_steps: Form two opposing, parallel lines with men in one line and women in the other, directly facing across the floor.
Engage the core and bend both knees to prepare an explosive vertical rebound.
Jump straight up off both feet, driving vertically into the air while keeping the torso upright and maintaining eye contact with the opposite line.
Land softly on the balls of both feet with knees flexed, keeping the rhythm steady.
Women step forward from their line to designate and dance facing their chosen partner.
teaching.formation: Two facing parallel lines: women on one side, men on the other.
teaching.level_notes: Requires strong leg conditioning, knee flexion, and aerobic endurance for repeated vertical jumping.
teaching.rhythm: Rhythmic accompaniment driven by the ngoma drum and ekitirikiti percussive cadence, punctuated by adungu melodic phrases.
